assumption: Active 18-34s feel the protein-vs-carbs-vs-real-food trade-off after training as a real pain (not a mild annoyance)
current_evidence: Founder reports people 'said yes to the idea' (unquantified); 9 interviews not yet shared
cheapest_test: Upload 9 interview notes + 20 more past-behaviour interviews (02 guide)
metric: % describing a specific recent post-training problem unprompted

assumption: People will pay ~£2.75 for an 80 g bar
current_evidence: Competitors sell at £2.50-2.95 (EVIDENCE: 02); our own buyers untested
cheapest_test: Waitlist price question + pilot sales at £2.75

assumption: Buyers repeat-purchase (it's not a one-off novelty)
cheapest_test: Paid pilot at 2 partners over 3 weeks

assumption: We can make a bar that tastes as good as what people buy now
cheapest_test: Blind taste test vs Grenade and Forza (n~20)

assumption: The calculated macros (~20 g P / ~37 g C / 5.2 g fibre) hold in a real bar
cheapest_test: Lab nutrition analysis of the hero bar

assumption: The bar stays soft and safe for >=4 weeks at room temperature
current_evidence: None; high-protein bars are known to harden
cheapest_test: 2- and 4-week keep test + water activity test
success_threshold: aw <=0.65; texture still acceptable at 4 weeks

assumption: Ingredient story ('no isolates, no sweeteners, no palm oil') influences purchase
current_evidence: RXBAR (simple-ingredient egg-white bar) left the UK (EVIDENCE: C20) - warning sign
cheapest_test: Interview Q10 + A/B two headline versions on landing page
metric: % citing ingredients as a reason; sign-up rate by headline

assumption: Clubs and gyms will stock or bulk-buy (Squad Box)
current_evidence: Pro clubs tied to SiS/Myprotein/Grenade (inherited); grassroots untested
metric: Partners agreeing to a pilot; reorder intent

assumption: ~23 g sugar per bar won't put off buyers
cheapest_test: Show label in taste test; ask about sugar
metric: % saying sugar would stop them buying

assumption: 5 g fibre straight after training causes no meaningful gut discomfort
current_evidence: Evidence base thin; no RCTs on post-exercise fibre (EVIDENCE: S1)

assumption: 'fettle' is free to use as a trade mark in classes 29/30
current_evidence: No clash found by web search; UK IPO not checked
cheapest_test: UK IPO + Companies House search (30 min)

assumption: Unit cost falls to ~£0.71 at co-man scale
metric: Quoted cost per bar at 10k MOQ

assumption: 'Recovery'/'refuel'/'real food' wording is acceptable to Trading Standards
current_evidence: Claims checked vs GB register; wording untested

assumption: Half-bar portioning is used and valued
metric: % who ate half and saved half
